findings.title: Stress-tier cost multipliers were never applied to booked PnL (tier1.5 stress is a duplicate of base; tier2.0 measures delay-only at base costs)
findings.detail: The frozen cost authority (w2_freeze cost_authority; accounting.bps_cost) specifies 1.5 bps/side x tiers {1.0,1.5,2.0} (1.50/2.25/3.00 USD per side on the 10k USD-unit). Neither family1.py nor family2.py trade dicts carry a 'cost_tier' field (verified in source: trade dicts contain trade_id/pair/side/notional_usd/entry_price/entry_ts/decision_ts/exit_price/exit_ts/exit_reason only), and scored_runner.book_trades books with cost_tier=tr.get('cost_tier', 1.0). Numeric proof from the ledger itself: implied per-side cost = exactly 1.500 bps in the base group AND the tier1.5 group of all 6 rows (e.g. family1:anchor base costs 4622.9999 USD = 1541 x 3.00 USD); tier1.5 metrics are byte-identical to base in all 6 cells. Consequently the ledger's stress.tier1.5 rows are exact copies of base, and stress.tier2.0 rows measure the frozen one-event fill delay at tier-1.0 costs, not the 3.0 bps/side cost stress.
findings.verdict_impact: NONE. All 6 cells fail EXPECTANCY_NONPOSITIVE at base; break_even_cost_bps is negative for all 6 (gross edge negative before any cost), so any higher cost tier makes expectancy strictly worse and no gate can flip to PASS. REJECT_ALL is robust a fortiori under the frozen cost authority. Recomputed gate_reasons match stored exactly.
